foreignObject.div: Figure 16. Direction 3's one correction package: the lever moved and the outcome did not follow. Five full-budget cells on the project_progressive_v1 schedule, 857,600 parameters and 24,000 steps, arm glu_source_v2. F5b's two (dashed, grey) ran with the shared input norm's gain left at its initialisation, 0.02; F5c's three (solid) set it once, at the predeclared feedback phase transition, to the token-frequency-weighted RMS of the embeddings the channel then meets. Right is the finding. The x axis is the quantity F5b's diagnosis named and the lever targets, and it moved 2.7×, from 0.27–0.29 to 0.74–0.80 — the fused input now arrives at the scale the trunk spent 24,000 steps learning to read. The y axis is the exact sequential soft−standard validation guard, and it did not come down: 49/63 before, 24/59/68 after, against a budget of +1.0 drawn in blue at the floor. Middle says the recurrence got worse, on the one axis the two packages may be compared on. Absolute likelihood cannot be compared — the packages use different data seeds and so different validation splits — but the repeated-prefill penalty is a within-checkpoint difference and the split cancels: 27 and 47 bits/drawing at pass 32 before, 100, 107 and 153 after, with no overlap. The most economical reading is that the small gain was not suppressing a good channel; it was keeping a bad one quiet. Left is the floor under all of it. The two clay curves are one configuration run twice with deterministic algorithms requested and granted by torch. They separate at the first eval — before the dashed rule where the calibration fires — and end 2.09 bits/drawing apart, with 8.7 bits/drawing between their guards and 1.5× between their wavefronts. That spread is comparable to the package-to-package differences in the middle panel and is not comparable to the 24–68× the guard misses its budget by, which is what makes the closure safe and the middle panel suggestive rather than settled. Three cells, no replicate within a seed, one schedule: a predeclared package answering one question, not an estimate of anything.
